title: Issuing equity shares by preferential allotment
law: Section 62(1)(c) with Rule 13 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Section 42 with Rule 14 and Section 39 with Rule 12 of the Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014
summary: The company offers new equity shares to a chosen group of people (not to all members) after getting a valuation, board approval and a special resolution, and then allots the shares.
when: When the company wants to raise money by issuing equity shares to selected investors, such as promoters, investors or lenders, instead of offering them to all existing members.
applies: Private and public companies (unlisted). Listed companies must also follow SEBI rules.

steps.d: See whether the Articles allow shares to be issued on a preferential basis. If not, alter the Articles by special resolution under Section 14. A Section 8 company limited by shares needs the Registrar's prior approval to alter its Articles.
docs: Special resolution to alter Articles (if needed)

steps.d: Send notice under Section 173 and SS-1 to all directors.
steps.time: At least 7 days, or shorter if the rules allow
docs: Notice, agenda and notes to agenda

steps.d: Appoint a registered valuer to give a valuation report. Authorise a director to take the steps needed for the proposed private placement of shares.
Once the valuation report arrives, send notice of a second board meeting.
steps.time: At least 7 days, or shorter if the rules allow

steps.d: Approve the offer cum application letter in Form PAS-4. Approve the issue, subject to the members' approval. Approve the general meeting notice. Approve opening a separate bank account to receive the subscription money.
docs: Draft notice of general meeting with explanatory statement

steps.t: File MGT-14 for the board resolution
steps.d: File MGT-14 with the Registrar and attach a certified true copy of the board resolution.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the board resolution
docs: Certified true copy of board resolution

steps.d: Issue notice under Section 101 and SS-2 with an explanatory statement giving the details required by Section 102, Sections 62 and 42 and Rule 14(1).
steps.time: At least 21 days, or shorter if members consent as the law allows

steps.d: Pass a special resolution for the preferential issue under Sections 62 and 42 and Rule 14(1).

steps.t: File MGT-14 for the special resolution
steps.d: File MGT-14 with the Registrar. Attach the certified true copy of the special resolution and the explanatory statement. If the Registrar queries, you may also need to attach the valuation report, notice with shorter notice consents, PAS-4 offer letter, meeting minutes with attendance sheet and scrutinizer report, and the list of members and directors.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the special resolution
docs: Certified true copy of special resolution

steps.d: Send notice of a board meeting to approve the allotment.
steps.time: At least 7 days, or shorter if the rules allow

steps.d: At the board meeting, allot the shares. Authorise issue of share certificates within 60 days if the shares are not in demat form. Credit demat accounts through a corporate action with the depositories. Authorise entry of the allottees in the register of members.
steps.time: Certificates within 60 days

steps.d: Pay stamp duty under the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 at 0.005% on the amount received for the shares.
File the return of allotment with a certified true copy of the allotment resolution and the list of allottees in the format given in Annexure A of the PAS-3 instruction kit on the MCA portal.
steps.time: Within 30 days of allotment
docs: Certified true copy of allotment resolution

steps.d: Give the details in the Board Report and in the Annual Return for the year of allotment. Put the information on the company website, if it has one.
Enter the allottees' names in the register of members under Section 88 and Rule 5.
steps.time: Within 7 days of allotment

forms.purpose: Private placement offer cum application letter
forms.deadline: Issue to the chosen persons after the special resolution

forms.purpose: Filing of board resolution and of special resolution
Return of allotment

checklist: Registered valuer appointed and valuation report received
General meeting notice with explanatory statement sent
Subscription money received through banking channels

meetings.title: Board meeting to appoint the valuer
Board meeting to approve the preferential offer and call the general meeting
Extraordinary general meeting for the preferential issue
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter with consent as the law allows)

meetings.title: Board meeting to allot the shares

resolutions.title: Appointment of a registered valuer and authority for the private placement
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT [name of valuer], a registered valuer registered with [registration number], be and is hereby appointed to value the equity shares of {co} for the proposed preferential issue under Sections 62(1)(c) and 42 of the Companies Act, 2013, on a fee of Rs. [amount]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director], Director, be and is hereby authorised to take all steps needed for the proposed private placement of equity shares.

resolutions.title: Approval of the preferential offer, issue and general meeting notice
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, having noted the valuation report dated [date], the offer cum application letter in Form PAS-4 be and is hereby approved, and equity shares of Rs. [face value] each be offered on a preferential basis to the persons named in the list placed before the Board at a price of Rs. [price] per share, subject to the approval of the members by special resolution under Sections 62(1)(c) and 42 of the Companies Act, 2013. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a general meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue] and the notice with explanatory statement placed before the Board be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a separate bank account be opened with [name of scheduled bank] to receive the subscription money, and [name of director] be authorised to operate it and to file e-Form MGT-14.

resolutions.title: Alteration of Articles to permit preferential issue (only if needed)
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013, the Articles of Association of {co} be altered by inserting the following new Article [number]: [text of article permitting issue of shares on a preferential basis]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file the necessary forms and to do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution.
resolutions.explanatory: This item is needed only if the existing Articles do not allow a preferential issue. The proposed new Article lets the company issue shares to chosen persons on terms approved by the members. The alteration will take effect from the date of this resolution. No director or key managerial personnel is interested except as members, to the extent of their shareholding.

resolutions.title: Issue of equity shares on a preferential basis
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Sections 62(1)(c) and 42 of the Companies Act, 2013, Rule 13 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, Rule 14 of the Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014 and the Articles of Association, the consent of the members be and is hereby given to the Board to offer, issue and allot [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each at Rs. [price] per share, including premium of Rs. [premium], on a preferential basis to [names of proposed allottees]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the allotment be completed within twelve months of the date of this resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to settle any question and do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution.
resolutions.explanatory: Particulars under Section 102, Section 62 and Rule 14(1): (a) object of the issue: [objects]; (b) total number of shares to be issued: [number]; (c) price at which allotment is proposed and the valuation report of [valuer] dated [date]; (d) basis on which the price was fixed; (e) name and relationship of the allottees, and the director or promoter intending to subscribe, if any; (f) shareholding pattern before and after the issue: [details]; (g) time within which the allotment will be completed: twelve months from this resolution; (h) change in control, if any: [details]. The valuation report is open for inspection at the registered office on working days. The Board recommends the resolution. Directors and key managerial personnel are interested only to the extent of any shares they or their relatives may subscribe: [details].

resolutions.title: Allotment of equity shares on a preferential basis
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Sections 62(1)(c), 42 and 39 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the special resolution passed on [date], [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each be and are hereby allotted at Rs. [price] per share to the allottees named in the list tabled at the meeting, against receipt of Rs. [amount] in the separate bank account. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT share certificates be issued within 60 days to allottees who hold shares in physical form, and the shares of other allottees be credited to their demat accounts through the depositories. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the names of the allottees be entered in the register of members, and [name of director] be authorised to file e-Form PAS-3.

docs.title: Consent to shorter notice of general meeting
paras: To the Board of Directors, {co}.

I, [name of member], holding [number] equity shares of {co}, consent to the general meeting to be held on [date] at [time] at [venue] being called at shorter notice, as allowed by Section 101 of the Companies Act, 2013.
Date: [date]. Signed: [name of member].

flags: The reference note does not mention Form PAS-5 (the record of the persons to whom offers are made). Rule 14(3) needs a record of offers in PAS-5, and it must be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of circulating the offer letter. Please verify.

The reference note does not mention the 60-day rule. Allotment must be completed within 60 days of receiving the money, or the money must be refunded within the next 15 days. Money must come only through banking channels, not cash.

The reference note places the PAS-4 approval before the general meeting. The offer letter should only be sent to the chosen persons after the special resolution is passed (and, as many practitioners check, after the MGT-14 is filed). Please confirm the order.

The reference note says MGT-14 is not needed for private placement by private companies. Exemptions for private companies from MGT-14 filing are narrow and have changed over the years. Verify the current rule before skipping the filing.

The reference note does not mention the cap of 200 persons per financial year or that offers must be to named persons, and does not mention that shares issued for non-cash consideration need a valuation. Check these.

title: Issuing equity shares by rights issue
law: Sections 62 and 179 of the Companies Act, 2013; Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Secretarial Standard on Board Meetings (SS-1)
summary: The company offers new equity shares to its existing equity members in proportion to what they hold, waits for acceptances, then allots the shares.
when: When the company wants more capital and prefers to offer the new shares first to its existing equity shareholders.
applies: All companies. Private companies get some relaxations on time periods. Listed companies must also follow SEBI rules.

steps.d: Send notice to all directors with the agenda, notes, and supporting papers. These include the draft letter of offer and the list of equity members with their percentage holdings.
steps.time: At least 7 days
docs: List of equity members with percentages

steps.d: Hold the meeting and approve the further issue by way of rights, in proportion to paid-up equity held on the date of offer. Authorise the Company Secretary or Managing Director to sign and send the letter of offer. The issue must be decided at a meeting, never by circulation (Section 179).

Test the real capital need and the price (par or premium). Approve the member list from the register of members or depository records. Check that the equity part of authorised capital is enough. Check the Articles for any limits on renouncing shares. If the Memorandum or Articles need change, follow that procedure first.
docs: Extract of register of members or depository list

steps.d: Prepare a letter for each equity member for the shares matching their holding. State the number of shares offered, date of offer, and opening and closing dates. State the acceptance period and say that silence means the offer is declined. State the right to renounce the shares in favour of another person.
steps.time: Acceptance period: 7 to 30 days from date of offer
docs: Letter of offer for each member

steps.d: Send each letter to the member's registered address by registered post, speed post, electronic mode, courier or any other mode that gives proof of delivery.
steps.time: At least 3 days before the issue opens

steps.t: Scrutinise responses and call the allotment meeting
steps.d: After the offer closes, check all acceptances, renunciations and declines (including deemed declines) against bank statements and cash vouchers. Prepare the list of allottees. Send notice of a board meeting with the bank statements, draft allottee list and the post-allotment shareholding.
steps.time: Board notice at least 7 days

steps.d: Pass resolutions to allot the shares. Authorise share certificates for physical shares, or intimation to depositories. Authorise filing of PAS-3. Direct the authorised person to update all registers.

Update the register of members with the rights issue and allotment details. Update the foreign register of members if one exists. Update the register of directors and key managerial personnel if an allottee is such a person. Update the register of significant beneficial owners if needed. Update attendance registers and minutes books for both board meetings.
steps.time: Register of members, directors and KMP, SBO register: within 7 days of allotment; foreign register: within 15 days

steps.d: File the return of allotment online with a copy of the allotment resolution certified by the Company Secretary or an authorised director and the list of allottees, and pay the fee.
steps.time: Within 30 days of allotment

steps.d: Issue and deliver share certificates, or inform depositories, for all allottees.
steps.time: Within 60 days of allotment

steps.d: After the offer period ends, or when a member declines earlier, the Board may place the declined shares in a way that does not harm the members or the company.

Show the rights issue in the Board Report and the change in share capital in the Annual Return. Listed companies must also make the disclosures SEBI requires. If a board meeting is held by video conferencing, follow the video conferencing rules.

forms.purpose: Return of allotment

checklist: List of equity members approved by the Board
Letter of offer states number, dates, acceptance period and right to renounce
Letters sent with proof of delivery at least 3 days before opening
Allotment decided at a board meeting, not by circulation
Share certificates or depository credit done

[face value] each at Rs. [price] per share (including premium of Rs. [premium]) by way of rights to the equity members of {co} on [date of offer], in the ratio of [ratio] equity shares for every [number] equity shares held. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the list of equity members and their holdings placed before the Board be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name], Company Secretary / Managing Director, be authorised to sign and send the letter of offer, with an acceptance period of [number] days from the date of offer, to each equity member, stating the right to renounce the shares in favour of another person.

resolutions.title: Allotment of shares issued by way of rights
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Section 62(1)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013, [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each be and are hereby allotted to the persons named in the list of allottees placed before the Board, against receipt of Rs. [amount]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT share certificates be issued under the seal (if any) and signature of two directors and the Company Secretary, or the depositories be informed, within 60 days. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registers be updated and [name of director] be authorised to file e-Form PAS-3 within 30 days of allotment.

docs.title: Letter of offer to an equity member
paras: To [name of member], [registered address]. Folio / DP ID and Client ID: [number].
Date of offer: [date]. Issue opens on: [date]. Issue closes on: [date].

{co} offers you [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each at Rs. [price] per share, in the proportion of [ratio] to the equity shares you hold, under Section 62(1)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013.

You may accept all or part of this offer. You may also renounce the shares offered, or any of them, in favour of another person, subject to the Articles of Association. To accept, send the acceptance form with payment of Rs. [amount] by [mode] to [bank details] before the issue closes.

If we do not receive your acceptance by the closing date, or you decline earlier in writing, the offer will be treated as declined. The Board may then place the shares in a manner that is not disadvantageous to the members and the company.

flags: The reference note gives the acceptance period as 7 to 30 days. Section 62(1)(a)(i) as originally enacted said 15 to 30 days, and the shorter period came through later changes. Verify the period in force today and for your type of company.

The reference note says a private company can use a shorter period (and shorter dispatch time) if 90% of members consent. The 90% consent relief comes from the 2015 private company exemption. Verify it is still in force and that the Articles do not conflict.
The reference note does not mention stamp duty on the new shares (0.005% on the issue amount, under the Indian Stamp Act, 1899). Check.

Rights shares also need the offer to reach all members in the manner the Rules require; the reference note does not mention e-forms like MGT-14 for the board resolution. Check whether it applies to your company.

title: Redeeming preference shares
law: Section 55 of the Companies Act, 2013; relevant provisions of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; terms of issue approved by the members
summary: The company pays back preference shareholders as the terms of issue allow, using profits or fresh share proceeds, and records the change.
when: When the redemption date of preference shares arrives, or the company decides to redeem them as the terms of issue allow.
applies: All companies that have issued redeemable preference shares

steps.d: Make sure the Articles allow redemption of preference shares. If not, alter them by special resolution under Section 14.
Check the redemption period, rate, mode and other terms. Make sure the shares can be redeemed under Section 55.
docs: Terms of issue of preference shares

steps.d: Under Section 55(2), redeem either out of profits that could otherwise be paid as dividend, or out of the proceeds of a fresh issue made for the purpose. If you use profits, you must create a Capital Redemption Reserve equal to the face value of the shares redeemed.
Approve the redemption. Approve the notice of a general meeting if member approval is needed (for example if there is a new issue or capital restructure). Authorise the filings and documents.

steps.t: Hold a general meeting if needed
steps.d: If the Articles must be altered, or new shares issued, or capital restructured, pass a special resolution. Pass an ordinary resolution for redemption if the terms need member approval.

steps.t: File PAS-3 if redeeming from a fresh issue
steps.d: File the return of allotment for the fresh shares.
steps.time: The reference note says 15 days of allotment

steps.d: Make sure profits or fresh issue proceeds are available. Work out any premium on redemption and pay it from profits or the securities premium account.
Pay the face value and any premium to the preference shareholders. Only fully paid shares can be redeemed; partly paid shares must be fully paid first.
If you redeemed from profits, transfer an amount equal to the face value redeemed to the Capital Redemption Reserve. That reserve can only be used to issue fully paid bonus shares.
The reference note lists Form SH-7 within 30 days. Show the redemption in the annual return (MGT-7 or MGT-7A) and in the financial statements filed in AOC-4 for that year.
steps.time: The reference note says 30 days for SH-7

steps.d: Update the register of members and the register of preference shareholders. Update the share capital in the books.
Show the amount redeemed, the reserve created and the source of funds. Follow Schedule III and make sure the audit reporting covers it.

forms.purpose: Return of allotment (only if redeeming from a fresh issue)

[face value] each, fully paid up, held by [names of holders], be redeemed at Rs. [amount per share] (including premium of Rs. resolutions.title: Approval of notice of general meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT a general meeting of {co} be held on [date] at [time] at [venue] to consider the items placed before the Board, and the notice with explanatory statement under Section 102 be approved and sent to the members, directors and auditors.

resolutions.title: Alteration of Articles to permit redemption of preference shares (only if needed)
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013, the Articles of Association of {co} be altered by adding Article [number]: [text permitting redemption of preference shares as per Section 55]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file the resolution and do all acts needed to give effect to it.
resolutions.explanatory: The present Articles do not clearly allow redemption of preference shares. The proposed Article lets the company redeem them as the terms of issue and Section 55 permit. No director or key managerial personnel is interested except as members, to the extent of their shareholding and any preference shares they hold: [details].

resolutions.title: Approval of redemption of preference shares by the members
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, as required by the terms of issue and under Section 55 of the Companies Act, 2013, the members approve the redemption of [number] [rate]% redeemable preference shares of Rs. [face value] each on [date] out of [profits / fresh issue proceeds], as approved by the Board on [date].
resolutions.explanatory: Needed only where the terms of issue call for member approval.

flags: The reference note says PAS-3 for a fresh issue is due within 15 days of allotment. Rule 12 of the Prospectus and Allotment Rules gives 30 days. Verify.

Form SH-7 is the notice of alteration of authorised share capital. Redemption normally reduces issued capital and needs no SH-7, unless you also change authorised capital. Check whether it is needed here.

Section 55 also bars issue of preference shares redeemable beyond 20 years (30 years for infrastructure projects) and needs redemption only of fully paid shares; confirm the terms of issue meet these.
A general meeting is not usually needed for redemption that follows terms already approved at issue. The reference note treats it as optional; confirm for your case.
The reference note mentions the register of preference shareholders; Section 88 does not name such a register separately. Check what your company keeps.

title: Issuing secured compulsorily convertible debentures (private company)
law: Section 71 with Rule 18 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Section 62 with Rule 13; Section 42 with Rule 14 of the Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014
summary: A private company raises money by issuing secured debentures that will convert into shares, with valuation, board and member approvals, a debenture trustee, a trust deed and a registered charge.
when: When a private company wants to raise funds from chosen investors through secured debentures that must convert into equity.
applies: Private companies (no specific relief for private companies in the reference note)

steps.d: Consider the proposal to issue securities and appoint a registered valuer.
steps.time: 7 days' notice or shorter notice as allowed

steps.d: Approve the issue of secured convertible debentures. Identify the persons to whom the offer will go. Approve the draft PAS-4 offer letter. Fix the date, time and venue of the general meeting and approve its notice. Note the valuer's report.

steps.t: File MGT-14 for the board resolution
steps.d: File MGT-14 with the Registrar for the board resolution approving the issue.
steps.time: Within 30 days

steps.d: Pass a special resolution to issue the debentures by preferential allotment. Allot within twelve months of the resolution.
steps.time: Allotment within 12 months

steps.t: File MGT-14 for the special resolution
steps.d: File MGT-14 with the Registrar.
steps.time: Within 30 days

steps.d: Open a separate account with a scheduled commercial bank to receive the money. Prepare the list of persons to receive the offer. The reference note says the offer letter can go out only after MGT-14 is filed.
Send the PAS-4 letter to the identified persons. Keep the record of private placement in Form PAS-5.
Accept payment only by cheque, demand draft or other banking channel, never cash. Keep a record of the bank account from which each payment came.
Appoint a debenture trustee before the offer letter goes out, to protect the debenture holders.
steps.time: Before issue of offer letter

steps.d: Allot the debentures. Approve the draft agreement for creating the charge and authorise a director to sign it. Approve the draft Debenture Trust Deed. Approve issue of debenture certificates signed by two directors.
steps.time: Within 60 days of receiving the money

steps.d: Create a charge or mortgage in favour of the debenture trustee on a specific movable property of the company, its holding, subsidiary or associate companies or others, or on specific immovable property or any interest in it. File CHG-9 with the Registrar.
steps.time: CHG-9 within 30 days of creating the charge

steps.d: File the return of allotment with the Registrar.
steps.time: The reference note says within 15 days of allotment

steps.d: Sign the trust deed in Form SH-12 in favour of the trustee. Give a copy to any member or debenture holder who asks within 7 days of the request, on payment of the fee.
steps.time: Within 3 months of closing of the issue (source also says 60 days of allotment)

steps.d: Because the debentures are compulsorily convertible, no debenture redemption reserve is needed (the reference note says so). For debentures that are not convertible, a reserve out of profits applies.
If securities are allotted for something other than cash, a registered valuer must value it and give a report with reasons.

[face value] each, to be converted into equity shares at [ratio / price formula] within [period], be approved. resolutions.title: Issue of secured compulsorily convertible debentures by preferential allotment
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Sections 62(1)(c), 62(3), 42 and 71 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the related Rules, the consent of the members be given to the Board to issue and allot [number] secured compulsorily convertible debentures of Rs. [face value] each, aggregating Rs. [amount], on a preferential basis to [names of allottees], convertible into equity shares on the terms set out in the explanatory statement. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the allotment be completed within twelve months of this resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to settle any question, create the security and do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution.
resolutions.explanatory: Particulars: (a) objects of the issue: [objects]; (b) number and face value of debentures: [details]; (c) terms of conversion, including price or formula and period; (d) valuation report of [valuer] dated [date], open for inspection; (e) names of the proposed allottees and their relationship, if any, to the company; (f) the security to be created: [description of property]; (g) shareholding before and after conversion: [details]; (h) time for allotment: twelve months from this resolution. The Board recommends the resolution. Directors and key managerial personnel are interested only to the extent of any debentures they may take: [details].

resolutions.title: Allotment of debentures, approval of charge and trust deed
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to the special resolution passed on [date], [number] secured compulsorily convertible debentures of Rs. [face value] each be allotted to the persons named in the list tabled before the Board, against receipt of Rs. [amount]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the draft agreement for creating a charge on [description of property] in favour of the debenture trustee and the draft Debenture Trust Deed be approved, and [name of director] be authorised to sign them. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT debenture certificates be issued under the signatures of two directors and [name], Company Secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file e-Forms CHG-9 and PAS-3.

flags: The reference note says PAS-3 is due within 15 days of allotment. Rule 12 gives 30 days. Verify.

The reference note says to appoint the trustee before the offer letter goes out and also says the trust deed is due within 60 days of allotment (step 10) and within three months of closing the issue (step 11). These do not match. Rule 18 says three months from the closing of the issue; confirm.

Section 71(5) needs a trustee when debentures go to more than 500 holders, or in the cases covered by Rule 18. The reference note says a private company issuing secured convertible debentures must appoint one; check Rule 18(1) for your case.

Compulsorily convertible debentures are treated as shares-in-waiting; the special resolution should also cover conversion terms (Section 62(3)) and check borrowing limits under Section 180(1)(c) for a public company. The reference note does not mention this.
The reference note says PAS-4 can go out only after the MGT-14 is filed. Check this against Rule 14 before relying on it.
Offers may go to at most 200 persons in a financial year, excluding qualified institutional buyers and employees under a scheme; the reference note does not say this.

title: Refusing to register a transfer of shares
summary: The Board decides to refuse a share transfer, records reasons, and tells the transferor and transferee in time, with their right to appeal.
when: When the company has received a signed share transfer form and the Board decides not to register it.
applies: Private companies and public companies. Public companies must give sufficient cause.

steps.d: Send the notice, agenda, notes and a letter saying that a signed share transfer form (SH-4) has been received.
steps.time: 7 days as per Section 173 and SS-1

steps.d: At the meeting, decide whether to approve or reject the transfer. Record the reasons in writing.
If the Board finds that registering the transfer would not be in the company's interest, pass a resolution refusing it.
Authorise a director to send the notice of refusal to the transferor and the transferee.
Send the notice to both parties with the reasons for refusal. Tell the transferee they can appeal to the NCLT within 30 days of receiving the notice.
steps.time: Within 30 days of receipt of the transfer instrument

steps.d: Follow Section 173 and SS-1 for the board meeting and the minutes.
A public company must send its notice within 30 days of receiving the transfer, give a valid and sufficient cause, and tell the transferee they can appeal to the NCLT within 60 days of the notice.
steps.time: Notice within 30 days; appeal within 60 days

forms.purpose: Securities transfer form received from the transferor

checklist: Notice sent to transferor and transferee within 30 days
Appeal rights stated in the notice

meetings.title: Board meeting to refuse the transfer of shares

resolutions.title: Refusal to register transfer of shares
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, having considered the share transfer form (SH-4) received on [date] for the transfer of [number] shares (distinctive nos. [from] to [to]) from [name of transferor] to [name of transferee], and for the reasons recorded in the minutes, namely [reasons], the Board, under Section 58(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Articles of Association, refuses to register the transfer. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to send a notice of refusal with reasons to the transferor and the transferee within 30 days of receipt of the transfer instrument, stating their right to appeal to the National Company Law Tribunal.

docs.title: Notice of refusal to register transfer of shares
paras: To [name of transferor] and [name of transferee]. Date: [date].

Notice under Section 58 of the Companies Act, 2013: {co} received the transfer form for [number] shares on [date]. The Board met on [date] and refused to register the transfer for these reasons: [reasons].
The transferee may appeal to the National Company Law Tribunal against this refusal within the time allowed by law, which is [30 / 60] days from receipt of this notice.
For {co}, [name], Director.

flags: Under Section 58, the first and third parts apply to private companies, while a public company's securities are meant to be freely transferable and the refusal route in Section 58(4) uses the 'sufficient cause' test. The reference note mixes both in one list; keep the private and public rules apart.
Step 4 in the reference note has a typo ('to transfer and transferee'). It should say the notice goes to the transferor and the transferee.

If no notice is sent within the period, the transferee may appeal within 60 days of delivery of the transfer instrument (90 days for a public company). The reference note gives this only in the next procedure.
For listed companies, SEBI rules on transfers and demat shares also apply.

title: Appeal to the NCLT against refusal to register a share transfer
law: Section 58 of the Companies Act, 2013; NCLT Rules, 2016
summary: A transferee or other aggrieved person appeals to the Tribunal when the company refuses, or fails, to register a transfer, and the Tribunal can order registration or rectification.
when: When a company refuses to register a transfer of shares, or does not act on it within 30 days.
applies: Private and public companies, with different time limits and some limits for private companies with transfer restrictions in their Articles

steps.t: Note the refusal and the time
steps.d: A company may refuse a transfer within 30 days of receiving the instrument, and must give reasons to the transferor and transferee. Count your time limit from the notice.
steps.time: Company acts within 30 days

steps.t: Know the time limits for appeal
steps.d: If the company refuses, appeal within 30 days of the refusal notice (60 days for a public company). If the company sends no response, appeal within 60 days (90 days for a public company) from the date the instrument was delivered to the company.
steps.time: 30/60 days from refusal; 60/90 days if no reply

steps.d: Use Form NCLT-1. Give details of the appellant and the respondent, the facts, the grounds, the reliefs sought and the documents attached (board resolution of refusal, transfer forms, copies of share certificates and similar). File with the NCLT bench that covers the company's registered office.
After filing, the appellant serves a copy on the company.
The NCLT sends a hearing notice to both sides. Each can appear through an authorised representative, company secretary or advocate.

After hearing, the NCLT may direct the company to register the transfer, or direct the register to be corrected and the company to pay any damages. It may also dismiss the appeal if the refusal was justified.
If the Tribunal rules for the appellant, the company must register the transfer.
steps.time: Within 10 days of receiving the order

steps.d: A person who breaks the Tribunal's order is punishable with imprisonment of 1 to 3 years and a fine of Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh.
Anyone unhappy with the NCLT order may appeal to the NCLAT.
steps.time: Within 45 days of the NCLT order

forms.purpose: Application or appeal to the NCLT
forms.deadline: As per the time limits above

checklist: Notice of refusal or proof of no reply
Date of delivery of transfer instrument noted
Appeal in NCLT-1 drafted with facts, grounds and reliefs

docs.title: Outline of appeal against refusal to register share transfer
paras: Before the National Company Law Tribunal, [bench]. In the matter of Section 58 of the Companies Act, 2013. [Name of appellant], [address], Appellant, versus {co}, [registered office address], Respondent.
Facts: The appellant is the transferee of [number] shares of {co}. The transfer form was delivered to the company on [date]. The company refused registration by notice dated [date] / sent no reply.
Grounds: [grounds, for example the refusal was without sufficient cause or without reasons, or the Articles allow free transfer].

Relief sought: (a) direction to the company to register the transfer; (b) rectification of the register of members; (c) damages of Rs. [amount], if any; (d) such other relief as the Tribunal thinks fit.
Annexures: board resolution of refusal, notice of refusal, share transfer form, share certificates, proof of delivery of the transfer instrument.

flags: The reference note says a transferee of a private company cannot appeal unless the Articles allow free transfer. Section 58(3) gives the transferee of a private company a right to appeal against a refusal. Restrictions in the Articles affect whether the Tribunal will order registration, but the right to appeal exists. Verify.

The reference note says Section 58(2) does not apply to private companies with transfer restrictions. Section 58(2) is the rule that a public company's securities are freely transferable; check the wording.
NCLT-1 is the general application form and fees apply under the NCLT Rules; check for the current procedure and e-filing.

title: Declaring beneficial interest in shares
law: Section 89 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 9 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014
summary: The person whose name is on the register and the person who really enjoys the shares each make a declaration to the company, and the company reports it to the Registrar.
when: When someone holds shares in the company's register but another person has the real benefit of them, or when that interest changes.
applies: All companies, though the reference note claims a limited relief for private companies

steps.d: A person has a beneficial interest if they enjoy the benefits of shares (dividends, voting rights, gains) without being the registered holder.

The registered owner makes a declaration naming the beneficial owner and giving particulars, with the date and nature of the arrangement. File MGT-4 with the company, with proof of identity of both persons.
steps.time: Within 30 days of being entered in the register or of a change in beneficial interest
docs: Proof of identity of both persons

steps.d: The beneficial owner states the number of shares, the nature of the interest, the registered owner's particulars and the date of acquisition. File MGT-5 with the company, with proof of identity of both persons.
steps.time: Within 30 days of acquiring the interest or of a change in it
docs: Proof of identity of both persons

steps.d: Hold a board meeting. Approve the declarations received in MGT-4 and MGT-5. Authorise a director to file MGT-6.
File MGT-6 with the Registrar with the board resolution and pay the fee under the Registration Offices and Fees Rules, 2014.
steps.time: Within 30 days of receiving the declaration

steps.d: Note the details in the register of members and other registers (Section 89(6) with Rule 9(3)).

forms.purpose: Declaration by registered owner
Declaration by beneficial owner
Return by the company to the Registrar
forms.deadline: Within 30 days of receiving the declaration

checklist: ID proofs of both persons attached

meetings.title: Board meeting to note declarations of beneficial interest

resolutions.title: Approval of declarations of beneficial interest and filing of MGT-6
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the declarations in Form MGT-4 received on [date] from [name of registered owner] and in Form MGT-5 received on [date] from [name of beneficial owner], regarding [number] shares of {co}, be noted and approved under Section 89 of the Companies Act, 2013. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file e-Form MGT-6 with the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of receipt of the declarations, and to make the entries in the register of members and other registers.

flags: The reference note lists conditions under which a private company need not file MGT-6 (not a subsidiary of a public company, filings up to date, same people, and no restriction in the charter documents). I do not know of such an exemption in Section 89 or Rule 9. Verify before relying on it.
The reference note says the registered owner files MGT-4 within 30 days of entry in the register. Check against Rule 9 whether the company also needs to see a declaration for every change.
Section 90 and the SBO Rules (BEN-1, BEN-2) are separate from Section 89; do not mix the two.

title: Conducting an extraordinary general meeting
law: Sections 100, 101, 108 and 118 of the Companies Act, 2013; Regulations 30, 44 and 47 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015; Secretarial Standard on General Meetings (SS-2)
summary: The Board calls the meeting, sends notice, runs the meeting, records minutes and files the required returns.
when: When the company needs member approval before the next annual general meeting.
applies: All companies. Listed companies have extra steps. Private companies get several relaxations.

steps.d: Send notice to all directors. Shorter notice may be given when business is urgent.
steps.time: At least 7 days

steps.d: Approve the date, time, venue and the explanatory statement. Obtain consent and appoint a scrutinizer for e-voting, fix the e-voting timeline, and decide the cut-off date for deciding who may vote. A listed company reports the board outcome to the stock exchange.
steps.time: Exchange intimation within 30 minutes of the board meeting (listed)

steps.d: Send notice with the explanatory statement to all members, directors and the auditor by registered post, email, electronic means or hand. If e-voting is offered, ordinary post cannot be used.
steps.time: At least 21 clear days

steps.d: Publish the notice in one English and one local-language newspaper, put it on the company website and send it to the stock exchange. If a record date is fixed, give notice of it to the exchange.
steps.time: Record date notice: at least 7 working days (per the reference note)

steps.d: The meeting may be held at shorter notice if not less than 95% of members entitled to vote consent in writing or electronically.

The Chairman of the Board, or a director the Board names, presides. If none is present, the members elect a chairman. The chairman runs the meeting fairly, explains the resolutions and lets members ask questions. Confirm that the quorum is present throughout.

For a public company, the quorum is 5 members present if there are up to 1000 members, 15 if there are 1001 to 5000, and 30 if there are more than 5000. For a private company it is two members present in person. If there is no quorum within half an hour, the meeting is adjourned to the same day, time and place the next week (or as the Articles say).
steps.time: Half an hour

steps.d: The scrutinizer reports to the chairman, who declares the result. Display the result at the registered office and on the website. A listed company sends the result to the exchange in the prescribed format and discloses the proceedings within 12 hours of the meeting.
steps.time: Listed: proceedings within 12 hours

steps.d: Write the minutes in the minutes book and have the chairman sign them. Include date, time and venue; names of members, directors and auditors present; the resolutions and any poll results; and the main points raised.
File MGT-14 with the Registrar for special resolutions. A listed company tells the exchange of the outcome and meets SEBI disclosure duties when the resolutions affect its securities.
steps.time: MGT-14 within 30 days of the meeting

forms.purpose: Filing of special resolutions with the Registrar

checklist: Board resolution on date, venue and notice
Notice with explanatory statement sent to members, directors and auditor
Newspaper and website notice done (if applicable)
Consents for shorter notice collected (if used)

meetings.title: Board meeting to call the extraordinary general meeting
Extraordinary general meeting
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter with 95% consent)

resolutions.title: Calling the extraordinary general meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT an extraordinary general meeting of {co} be held on [date] at [time] at [venue / video conference link] to transact the business set out in the notice placed before the Board, and the notice with explanatory statement under Section 102 of the Companies Act, 2013 be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name], a [practising professional], be appointed scrutinizer for the e-voting and voting at the meeting, and [date] be fixed as the cut-off date for deciding the members entitled to vote. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / Company Secretary] be authorised to sign and send the notice and do all acts needed.

resolutions.title: [Subject of the ordinary resolution]
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to [section / rule], the approval of the members of {co} be given to [describe the business]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution.
resolutions.explanatory: Explain the reason for the business, the directors' and key managerial personnel's interest in it, and any papers open for inspection.

resolutions.title: [Subject of the special resolution]
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to [section / rule] of the Companies Act, 2013, the approval of the members of {co} be given by special resolution to [describe the business]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file the resolution with the Registrar and do all acts needed to give effect to it.
resolutions.explanatory: Explain the reason for the business, the directors' and key managerial personnel's interest in it, and any papers open for inspection.

docs.title: Consent to shorter notice of general meeting
paras: To {co}.
I, [name of member], holding [number] shares, consent to the extraordinary general meeting on [date] at [time] at [venue] being held at shorter notice under Section 101 of the Companies Act, 2013.
Date: [date]. Signed: [name].

flags: The reference note gives 'at least 7 working days' for record date notice. A companion procedure in the same set says 3 working days. Check Regulation 42 of the SEBI LODR rules in force.
The reference note says 95% consent for shorter notice. Section 101 says a majority in number of members who also hold at least 95% of the paid-up capital (or voting power). Verify.
The reference note says MGT-14 for special resolutions only. Section 117 also covers some other resolutions.

The reference note says quorum is 'typically' by members present; Section 103 sets it as members personally present. The adjournment rule applies to a public company under Section 103(2); check the Articles for a private company.
The reference note's list of 'steps not applicable to private companies' ends with unnumbered items J and K. These look like leftovers; ignore them.

title: Getting a Director Identification Number (DIN)
law: Section 153 of the Companies Act, 2013; Rule 9(1) of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014; Rule 10 of the LLP Rules, 2009
summary: An individual gets a unique DIN, either with the incorporation form of a new company or through Form DIR-3 for an existing company or LLP.
when: When a person is to be appointed as a director of a company, or designated partner of an LLP, and does not already have a DIN.
applies: All companies and LLPs. Each person may hold only one DIN.

steps.d: If the person is to be a first director of a company being incorporated, use SPICe+ Part B. If the person is to join an existing company, use Form DIR-3.

steps.t: New company: file SPICe+ Part B
steps.d: File SPICe+ Part B on the MCA portal. Up to 3 DINs can be allotted through this form. Attach proof of identity (PAN for Indians, passport for foreigners), proof of address, a passport-size photograph and the declaration in Form DIR-2.
The DIN is allotted when the SPICe+ Part B form is approved.

Log in to the MCA portal and fill in DIR-3. Attach a photograph, a self-attested PAN (Indians) or passport (foreigners), a self-attested identity proof and a self-attested residence proof such as a postpaid mobile bill, bank statement or utility bill. The reference note also lists a board resolution proposing the appointment.
Verify the mobile number and email address by OTP. Enter the CIN, FCRN, LLPIN or FLLPIN of the entity in which the person is to be director or partner.
The applicant and an authorised director of the company concerned must both sign DIR-3 with their digital signature certificates. Download the form, attach the signatures and upload it.
Pay the fee (Rs. 500 at the time of the reference note). MCA processes the form, and the DIN is sent by email on approval.
The director tells the company about the DIN within 30 days. The company then informs the Registrar in DIR-12.
steps.time: Within 30 days

steps.d: A DIN is valid for life unless deactivated, surrendered or cancelled. The director must file DIR-3 KYC every year.
steps.time: By 30 September each year

forms.purpose: DIN for first directors of a new company (up to 3)
Consent and declaration of the proposed director
Application for DIN for an existing company or LLP
Notice to the Registrar of appointment of director
Yearly KYC to keep the DIN active

checklist: DSC of applicant and company director available
DIN received and told to the company
flags: The reference note names a form DIR-3B for the director to intimate the DIN to the company. I do not recognise this as a prescribed form; Section 156 only needs the director to inform the company in writing within one month. Verify.

The reference note says the penalty for holding multiple DINs is up to Rs. 50,000 plus Rs. 500 a day. Section 159 provides for imprisonment up to six months or a fine of Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 1 lakh, or both. Verify.
The DIR-3 route has changed several times (portal versions, whether a board resolution is attached, fee). Check the current MCA instruction kit.
DIR-3 KYC is due by 30 September each year. A late filing results in deactivation of the DIN and a fee to reactivate; confirm the current fee.

title: Approving director pay when profits are low or absent
law: Sections 197 and 198 and Schedule V of the Companies Act, 2013; Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
summary: When profits are inadequate, the company may still pay directors up to the Schedule V limits with an ordinary resolution, or above the limits with a special resolution.
when: When a public company has no profits or profits less than the remuneration it wants to pay its managing, whole-time or other directors.
applies: Public companies. Sections 196(4), 196(5) and 197 do not apply to private companies.

steps.d: Section 197(3) with Schedule V sets the maximum pay for directors, including a managing director, whole-time director, manager and non-executive directors, when profits are inadequate or absent.
The Act does not define inadequate profits. It means profits less than the total pay proposed to the directors. Then pay must follow Section II of Schedule V.

Approve the pay of all directors on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, if one exists. Get Audit Committee approval too where the pay goes to promoter or promoter group directors. Approve the general meeting notice and explanatory statement.
steps.time: 7 days' notice or shorter

steps.d: Include the information Schedule V needs: general information about the company, background and past pay of the appointee, experience and job profile, reasons for inadequate profits and similar details.
Pass an ordinary resolution to pay within the Table limits of Section II of Schedule V. Pass a special resolution to pay above those limits.

Yearly limits by effective capital. Negative or below Rs. 5 crore: Rs. 60 lakh for a managerial person and Rs. 12 lakh for another director. Rs. 5 crore to below Rs. 100 crore: Rs. 84 lakh and Rs. 17 lakh. Rs. 100 crore to below Rs. 250 crore: Rs. 120 lakh and Rs. 24 lakh. Rs. 250 crore and above: Rs. 120 lakh plus 0.01% of effective capital above Rs. 250 crore, and Rs. 24 lakh plus the same 0.01%. A professional may be paid under these limits.
If a special resolution is passed, file MGT-14 with the certified copy and explanatory statement.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the special resolution
docs: Certified true copy of special resolution

steps.d: Listed entities disclose pay details in the corporate governance report: all pay elements, fixed and performance-linked parts with criteria, and stock option details. Disclose pay of the managerial person and other directors in the annual return. Put the notice and explanatory statement on the website, if any.

forms.purpose: Filing of special resolution

checklist: Board approved notice and explanatory statement
Resolution passed (ordinary within limits, special above)
Annual return and corporate governance disclosures planned

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve director pay and call the general meeting
General meeting to approve remuneration
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter with consent as the law allows)

resolutions.title: Approval of remuneration in case of inadequate profits and call of general meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee [and with the approval of the Audit Committee] and pursuant to Sections 197 and 198 and Schedule V of the Companies Act, 2013, remuneration of Rs. [amount] per year be paid to [name], [designation], for the period [from] to [to], subject to the approval of the members. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT, as the company has inadequate profits, a general meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue], and the notice and explanatory statement placed before the Board be approved.

resolutions.title: Payment of remuneration within Schedule V limits
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Sections 197 and 198 and Section II of Part II of Schedule V of the Companies Act, 2013, approval be given to pay [name], [designation], remuneration of Rs. [amount] per year for [period], being within the limits in Schedule V, even if the company has inadequate profits or no profits. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to vary the terms within these limits.
resolutions.explanatory: Give the information required by Schedule V: general information about the company; the appointee's background, past pay, recognition or awards, and job profile; the remuneration proposed and its comparison with similar posts; reasons for inadequate profits and steps taken to improve them; and other disclosures.

resolutions.title: Payment of remuneration above Schedule V limits
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Sections 197 and 198 and Schedule V of the Companies Act, 2013, approval be given to pay [name], [designation], remuneration of Rs. [amount] per year for [period, not more than three years], which is above the limits in Schedule V, even if the company has inadequate profits or no profits. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution and file the required forms.
resolutions.explanatory: Give the information required by Schedule V and also explain why pay above the limits is needed: appointee's background and past pay, proposed pay, comparison with similar posts, reasons for inadequate profits, steps taken to improve profits, and the period of the approval. Directors and KMP are interested only to the extent of their own pay.

flags: Item (c) and (b) in the reference note's disclosure list are the same text repeated, which looks like a copy error.
The reference note heading says disclosure in the Board Report and Annual Return, yet the list is for the corporate governance report. Check the actual disclosure needs for your type of company.
A special resolution for pay above Schedule V limits normally covers a period of not more than three years; the reference note does not say this. Verify.
Schedule V also sets conditions about default in paying dues to banks, creditors and others; the reference note does not mention these. Check them.
The reference note's note under C lists situations where Section II does not apply. Confirm the details (for example new companies for seven years) against Schedule V before relying on them.

title: Calling an extraordinary general meeting by the Board
law: Sections 100 to 120 of the Companies Act, 2013; Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014; SS-1 and SS-2 (effective 1 April 2024); SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015 (Regulations 30, 42, 46); MCA circular of 8 April 2020 and later circulars for VC meetings; exemption notification of 5 June 2015 for private companies
summary: A full step-by-step plan for the Board to call, hold and follow up an extraordinary general meeting, including e-voting, listed company filings and video conferencing meetings.
when: When the Board wants to put a matter to the members before the next annual general meeting.
applies: All companies. Listed companies have extra steps. Some provisions are relaxed for private companies.

steps.d: Appoint a scrutinizer and arrange e-voting if it applies (listed companies and companies with 1,000 or more members). The scrutinizer is a practising CA, CS, CMA or advocate who has given consent. E-voting stays open at least 3 days and closes at 5 p.m. the day before the meeting. Fix the date, time and venue, allowing 21 clear days' notice. The venue must be in India, except for a wholly owned subsidiary of a foreign company. Prepare a route map unless the members are only directors or their relatives or the company is a wholly owned subsidiary. Choose physical or video mode.

Include meeting number, day, date, time, venue, agenda, resolution drafts with their type, explanatory statement, e-voting steps, proxy form and attendance slip. For a managing or whole-time director appointment, include terms and pay. Every item is special business.

Draft resolutions to fix the meeting, approve the notice, authorise a person to sign and send it, appoint the scrutinizer and e-voting agency, authorise the chairman to receive the report, fix the record date and fix the cut-off date, which must be no earlier than 7 days before the meeting.
Send notice to all directors at their registered addresses and pass the resolutions. The Board may also pass them by circulation under SS-1.
steps.time: At least 7 days' notice (shorter if urgent)

steps.d: Report the board outcome to the exchange and post it on the website. If the meeting ends after trading hours but more than 3 hours before the next trading day opens, report within 3 hours of closure.
steps.time: Within 30 minutes of the meeting; website within 2 working days

steps.d: Finalise and enter the minutes in the minute book as SS-1 requires.

Decide how to send the notice (ordinary, speed or registered post, email or electronic means; not ordinary post if e-voting is used). Make the list of members on the record date and of other people entitled to notice: directors, statutory auditors, secretarial auditors, debenture trustees and others the law names, with the RTA's help. A listed company gives the exchange record date notice.
steps.time: Listed: record date notice at least 3 working days (per the reference note)

steps.d: Send the notice to all members and others entitled. A listed company also sends it to the exchanges and posts it on its website. It may also publish in a newspaper (the rule requiring this was removed in 2024).
steps.time: At least 21 clear days (shorter if members consent); website and exchange within 2 working days

steps.d: Keep a register of proxies. Record proxies received at least 48 hours before the meeting in order, with reasons for any rejection. Have the notice, ballot form, register of members and proxy register at the venue. Arrange a poll if members demand it. Collect any shorter notice consents before the meeting.
steps.time: Proxies at least 48 hours before

steps.d: Confirm quorum under Section 103 and SS-2 throughout. The Chairman takes the chair. If absent 15 minutes after the time, the directors elect a chair, then members if no director will. The chairman explains any director's absence. Directors and the Company Secretary sit with the chairman. The chairman conducts only the business in the notice, regulates voting, and closes with a vote of thanks.

Keep the recorded transcript safe and, for a public company, post it on the website. Offer two-way video for at least 1000 members and open the link 15 minutes early. No proxies. Members who did not e-vote may vote by show of hands. Include the MCA circular framework in the notice.
File all resolutions passed with the Registrar in MGT-14. The reference note says 60 days; see flags.
steps.time: Reference note: 60 days

steps.d: A listed company tells the exchange the proceedings within 12 hours and posts them on the website within 2 working days. The scrutinizer reports to the chairman within 3 days. Display the result for at least 3 days at the registered, corporate and head offices and on the website. A listed company files the voting results with the exchange in SEBI's format within 2 working days. The scrutinizer keeps the register and papers until the chairman signs the minutes and then hands them over.
steps.time: Scrutinizer report within 3 days; exchange results within 2 working days

steps.d: Prepare the minutes and enter them in the minute book as SS-2 requires. File other returns for resolutions passed, such as DIR-12 and MGT-14.

forms.purpose: Filing of resolutions with the Registrar
forms.deadline: The reference note says 60 days; Section 117 says 30 days

checklist: Date, time, venue and mode fixed
Draft notice, proxy form and attendance slip ready
Member list on record date ready
Notice sent to members, directors, auditors and others

meetings.title: Board meeting to call the extraordinary general meeting
Extraordinary general meeting
meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter with consent as the law allows)

resolutions.title: Calling the extraordinary general meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT an extraordinary general meeting of {co} be held on [date] at [time] at [venue / video link] under Sections 100 and 101 of the Companies Act, 2013, and the notice with explanatory statement placed before the Board be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / Company Secretary] be authorised to sign and send the notice. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name], [qualification], be appointed scrutinizer and [name of agency] be appointed for remote e-voting, and the Chairman or, in his absence, any director be authorised to receive the scrutinizer's report and papers. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [date] be fixed as the record date and [date], not earlier than 7 days before the meeting, as the cut-off date for e-voting.

resolutions.title: [Subject of the ordinary resolution]
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to [section / rule] of the Companies Act, 2013, approval of the members of {co} be given to [describe the business]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution.
resolutions.explanatory: Explain the reason for the item, the interest of directors and key managerial personnel, and any papers open for inspection.

resolutions.title: [Subject of the special resolution]
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to [section / rule] of the Companies Act, 2013, approval of the members of {co} be given by special resolution to [describe the business]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director] be authorised to file the resolution with the Registrar and do all acts needed to give effect to it.
resolutions.explanatory: Explain the reason for the item, the interest of directors and key managerial personnel, and any papers open for inspection.

docs.title: Consent to shorter notice of general meeting
paras: To the Board of Directors, {co}.
I, [name of member], holding [number] shares, consent to the extraordinary general meeting on [date] at [time] at [venue] being held at shorter notice under Section 101 of the Companies Act, 2013.
Date: [date]. Signed: [name].

flags: The reference note says MGT-14 is due within 60 days. Section 117(1) gives 30 days (late filing allowed with additional fees). Verify.

The reference note says record date notice is 3 working days. The companion EGM procedure says 7 working days, and Regulation 42 of the SEBI LODR rules has asked for longer notice than 3 working days in recent versions. Check the current rule.
The reference note says shorter notice is allowed 'if the Articles so permit'. Section 101 allows shorter notice on consent of the required members and does not depend on the Articles. Verify.

The reference note says Sections 101 to 107 and 109 do not apply to private companies if the Articles provide otherwise. I recall the 2015 private company exemption as narrower and keeping Section 102 (explanatory statement) in place. Check the notification text.
MCA circulars on VC for EGMs have been extended repeatedly; check whether they are still in force.
Steps 8 and 28 mention SS-1 and SS-2 with an effective date of 1 April 2024; verify against the version currently notified.
